prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (alias Morrowick), export link to external Grid Interface Relay (gives normal-supply/protection status indications); public grid, non-farm port ops out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (alias Glassfin; authorized control within limits; blocks commands conflicting with protection; produces Pitch Deviation Notice; enters safe mode if auxiliary services unavailable), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (alias Larkspur; blade imagery; suspended if unsafe). Substation: Main Transformer, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers (feed auxiliary loads from MV collection; essential/nonessential separated), Emergency Generator (alias Foxglove) feeding emergency distribution bus (Morrowick keeps it within limits). Aux power: on normal loss, auto start; transfer only when voltage/frequency within limits; no parallel sources without approved synchronizing; not for export; loads prioritized (safety, protection, shutdown); nonessential auto-shed on overload; start/stabilize failure raises alarm, keeps UPS control power; recovery procedure restores normal supply; scheduled exercising and readiness checks (fuel, cooling, lubrication, battery, exhaust). Shore: SCADA Gateway (alias Juniper Vale; shows status; flags work packages from Pitch Deviation Notice; status to permit reviewers; sends supply alarms/generator status to Shore Control Room), Shore Control Room (alias Amber Quay), Maintenance Planning Engine (alias Thistle Crown; schedules from condition/history), Fleet Dispatch Console (alias Sable Orchard). Vessels: Crew Transfer Vessel (alias Kestrel Bay), Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel; Helideck; Vessel AIS Receiver (alias Blue Granite; produces Position Quality Flag). Personnel Tracking Console; North/South Access Scanners; Warehouse System (alias Mosslight; Backorder Exception Slip); Spares Hub; Metocean Buoy (alias Copper Finch; Wave Burst Record at sampling interval). Cybersecurity Gateway (alias Quiet Harbor): deny-by-default, RBAC, logged time-limited privileged sessions, segmentation, retest after changes. Remote commands authorized, recorded; local protection priority. Work Permit Portal (alias Redoubt): request→Duty Planner queues→reviews (HSE Officer, technical, Marine Coordinator, Vessel Master)→approval after recorded reviews, scoped→Field Supervisor verifies; change requires reassessment→completion, closure, audit records. Actors: Duty Planner (Transfer Manifest

New part:
S195: Thistle Crown schedules periodic reviews of standby electrical maintenance requirements and outstanding corrective work.
S196: After normal supply is restored, transfer back is permitted only after stable conditions are confirmed and the emergency source can be unloaded safely.
S197: The Grid Interface Relay defines the operational boundary between the offshore farm and the external transmission system.
S198: Grid Interface Relay is known operationally as Wildmere.
S199: The farm exports electrical power through the Offshore Substation, Main Transformer, and export cable to the designated grid connection point.
S200: The Export Cable Monitor provides measurements that support assessment of the export path.
S201: The Grid Interface Relay exchanges authorized operating signals with the transmission system at the agreed interface.
S202: The Grid Dispatcher sets external dispatch requirements within the applicable connection agreement.
S203: The Fleet Dispatch Console allocates requested farm output among available generating units.
S204: Dispatch commands remain subject to equipment capability, protection settings, and approved operating limits.
S205: The farm reports measured active power at the grid boundary for operational monitoring and settlement processes.
S206: Reactive power capability is managed in accordance with the connection agreement and current equipment conditions.
S207: Frequency response functions are enabled only when the relevant operating mode is authorized and available.
S208: Protection coordination prevents a fault on the external system from causing unnecessary disconnection of healthy farm equipment.
S209: Loss of communications does not remove local electrical protection or equipment interlocks.
S210: A Grid Constraint may require reduced export, revised dispatch, or temporary disconnection.
S211: SCADA Gateway provides relay status and interface measurements to the farm monitoring environment.
S212: SCADA Gateway produces the Session Revocation Receipt when an authenticated control session is terminated.
S213: Maintenance Planning Engine uses the Squall Window Bulletin when reviewing the timing of planned work.
S214: Amber Quay coordinates operational notices and control-room decisions affecting the farm interface.
S215: Kestrel Bay reports its approach and departure status in accordance with the approved marine coordination procedure.
S216: The Substation Operator confirms that switching actions affecting the export path are within the authorized work scope.
S217: The Control Engineer verifies that dispatch changes are reflected in the applicable control settings before implementation.
S218: Interface alarms are prioritized according to their effect on safety, equipment protection, and continuity of export.
S219: Planned tests are coordinated to avoid conflicting with dispatch obligations or active maintenance work.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
